correctness.rationale: The all-size induction proves the relative separation criterion for a marked coloured equivalence structure, including both existing-class colour requests and both new-class requests. Each monochromatic projection has an exact uncoloured rank staircase, forcing total order \(t(t+1)\). At equality, the unique largest red and blue classes force either a \((t,t)\) joint class with a level-\(t-1\) residual or the crossed classes \((t,t-1),(t-1,t)\) with level-\(t-2\) residual; both branches are sufficient by the same separation lemma. The two disjoint cases yield \(a_t=a_{t-1}+a_{t-2}\), with \(a_0=1,a_1=2\). Independent defining-game recursion and exhaustive forced-pairing enumeration were run from the supplied executable, not used in place of the induction. The result is limited to finite hosts.

value.rationale: This is a sharp full-rank-threshold host-size classification in a natural non-free-amalgamation hereditary class, supplemented by every extremal colour-preserving isomorphism type and the nontrivial Fibonacci enumeration. Independent marginal staircases allow false positives; the joint recursion resolves that structural gap for all ranks. The classification gives explicit smallest witnesses and a basis for comparison with extensions to more named colours.
